name: EZFlora
description: An 8-zone irrigation controller with 4 program schedules. It runs one zone at a time, can use zone 8 as a pump zone, and can stop watering when its rain sensor input says it's raining.

verification.note: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) gives 0x04/0x00 to the Compacta EZRain Sprinkler Controller and lists no EZFlora; the HouseLinc device catalog gives the same identity to the EZRain as model 31270. That the EZFlora reports it is read from those entries: no other irrigation controller from Compacta is listed, and no EZFlora document gives a category.

steps.text: Connect one wire of each valve to a Zone 1 to 8 terminal and the other to a Comm terminal. For more than one valve, connect all the common wires together and run one lead from them back to a Comm terminal.
Connect a 24 V AC power supply to the two AC Xmr terminals.
Plug in the EZFlora.
Plug the 24 V AC transformer into a 120 V AC outlet.

notes: Each zone drives one valve, 500 mA at most.
Make the power connections indoors or in weatherproof enclosures.

steps.text: Press and hold the controller's button, such as a KeypadLinc button, until it begins to blink.
Press and hold the SET button for about 4 seconds.
steps.expect: LED goes out; the controller stops blinking

steps.text: Tap the SET button once for zone 1, twice for zone 2, and so on.
Press and hold the SET button for about 4 seconds.

notes: The EZFlora links as a responder; repeat the steps for each zone, with its own controller button.

To control the zones with X10 instead, the unit code picks the zone (A1 for zone 1, A8 for zone 8): press and hold the SET button for about 4 seconds (the LED blinks steadily), then send the X10 command, such as A1 On, 3 times within 30 seconds. Sending Off in its place disables X10. The EZFlora Insteon and X10 Messages/Commands add that the house code is chosen on the X10 controller and that any unit code enables it.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button for about 4 seconds.
Tap the SET button once, for zone 1.
Press and hold the SET button for about 4 seconds.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, for zone 1; the device makes no link back to the Hub, since this profile lists no group it controls.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub. The EZFlora Insteon and X10 Messages/Commands list ID Request and Ping.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 10 seconds.

notes: The documents don't say whether the controller goes into unlinking mode first, how a zone is chosen, or what the LED shows.

verification.note: Read from the EZFlora Insteon and X10 Messages/Commands, which give Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) as the same as holding the SET button for 10 seconds; the Quick Start Guide - EZFlora Model #5010A gives no unlinking steps.

steps.text: Unplug the EZFlora.
Wait at least 5 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button while plugging it back in.
Keep holding the SET button for 5 seconds.
Release the SET button.
Unlink the device from every controller it is linked to.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: Each zone has a maximum run of 30 minutes, so a missed Off doesn't leave it running. Zone 8 can be set up as a pump zone that turns on with any other zone. Timers and programs need a gateway or software to set up.

The RJ-45 accessory port isn't for data or Ethernet. For a rain sensor, connect a 4.7 kΩ resistor between pins 2 and 6 and the sensor between pins 6 and 7; for a water meter, connect it between pins 4 and 5. Both must be enabled in the configuration register.
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)
